body:
Found during the adversarial review of #341, by checking each label's stated hydration number against the known stable hydrates of that salt.

| record label | stated n | known hydrates |
|---|---|---|
| `CaCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 1, 2, 4, 6 |
| `CuCl2 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2 |
| `FeCl2 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2, 4 |
| `FeCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 2, 4 |
| `FeCl3 x 4 H2O` | 4 | 6 |
| `MgCl2 x 7 H2O` | 7 | 6 |
| `Na2HPO4 x 3 H2O` | 3 | 2, 7, 8, 12 |
| `Na2HPO4 x 6 H2O` | 6 | 2, 7, 8, 12 |
| `NiCl2 x 5 H2O` | 5 | 2, 4, 6 |

10 of the 19 checked do match a known hydrate, so this is not a systematic notation problem — it is 9 specific labels.

## The pattern worth chasing first

`MgCl2 x 7 H2O` and `FeCl2 x 7 H2O` stand out: **`MgSO4·7H2O` and `FeSO4·7H2O` are among the most common salts in microbial growth media**, and both are genuine heptahydrates. A sulfate → chloride slip somewhere upstream would produce exactly these two labels. Worth checking the source rows before assuming the hydration number is what's wrong — it may be the anion.

Note MIM already holds separate `FeSO4 x 7 H2O` records (`CHEBI:75832`/`CHEBI:75836` appear as a same-name-different-identifier pair in the duplicate report), so a comparison against those recipes is possible.

## Relationship to #341

#341 corrected these records' `molecular_formula` from the anhydrous salt's to one that includes the stated water, so for these 9 the formula now faithfully encodes a hydration number that may not correspond to a real substance. That is **not a regression** — the previous value (the anhydrous formula) was wrong for every hydrate — but it does mean the formula is only as good as the label, and these 9 labels are in question.

Resolving this needs the upstream source rows (MediaDive / CultureBotHT / the original recipe text), not chemistry reasoning, so it was filed rather than guessed at.

comments.body:
## Source data found — and my sulfate→chloride hypothesis is wrong

I filed this suggesting `MgCl2 x 7 H2O` and `FeCl2 x 7 H2O` looked like `MgSO4`/`FeSO4·7H2O` slips introduced upstream. **That is refuted.**

MediaDive's REST API (`https://mediadive.dsmz.de/rest/ingredients`, 1244 ingredients) is the upstream source for these records, and **all 9 labels exist there verbatim**:

| MediaDive ingredient | formula | mass | CAS-RN |
|---|---|---|---|
| `CaCl2 x 6 H2O` *(real hydrate)* | `CaCl2H12O6` | 219.076 | 7774-34-7 |
| **`CaCl2 x 7 H2O`** | `CaCl2` | **110.983** | 10043-52-4 |
| `FeCl2 x 4 H2O` *(real)* | `Cl2FeH8O4` | 198.812 | 13478-10-9 |
| **`FeCl2 x 6 H2O`** | `Cl2Fe` | **126.75** | 7758-94-3 |
| **`FeCl2 x 7 H2O`** | `Cl2Fe` | **126.75** | 7758-94-3 |
| `FeCl3 x 6 H2O` *(real)* | `Cl3FeH12O6` | 270.296 | 10025-77-1 |
| **`FeCl3 x 4 H2O`** | `Cl3Fe` | **162.203** | 7705-08-0 |
| `MgCl2 x 6 H2O` *(real)* | `Cl2H12MgO6` | 203.303 | 7791-18-6 |
| **`MgCl2 x 7 H2O`** | `Cl2Mg` | **95.21** | **None** |
| `CuCl2 x 2 H2O` *(real)* | `Cl2CuH4O2` | 170.483 | 10125-13-0 |
| **`CuCl2 x 6 H2O`** | `Cl2Cu` | **134.452** | 7447-39-4 |
| **`Na2HPO4 x 3 H2O`**, **`x 6 H2O`** | `H3O4P.2Na` | **141.959** | 7558-79-4 |
| **`NiCl2 x 5 H2O`** | `Cl2Ni` | **129.599** | 7718-54-9 |

So MIM did not introduce these labels and there is no anion mix-up. They are faithful copies of what MediaDive publishes.

## What MediaDive's own data says

For all 9, MediaDive assigns the **anhydrous** formula, the **anhydrous mass**, and the **anhydrous CAS** — i.e. it records the label but does not resolve it to a distinct hydrate. `MgCl2 x 7 H2O` has **no CAS at all**, which is what you would expect for a substance that does not exist.

The signal is suggestive rather than clean: `NiCl2 x 6 H2O` and `Na2HPO4 x 12 H2O` are *genuine* hydrates that also carry anhydrous mass in MediaDive, so its hydrate coverage is simply patchy. But every one of the 9 falls on the anhydrous side.

## The consequence for MIM, which is the part that needs a decision

In #349 I appended water to these formulas from the stoichiometry the label states, so MIM now publishes e.g. `Ca.2Cl.7H2O` — **a mass for a substance the upstream source declines to characterise and that has no known existence.**

Three options:

1. **Revert these 9 to the anhydrous formula**, matching MediaDive. Aligns MIM with its source, but is wrong by ~108 g/mol if the recipe really did mean a hydrate.
2. **Keep the constructed hydrate formula** and annotate each record that the hydration number is unattested. Wrong by ~18 g/mol against the nearest real hydrate.
3. **Clear `molecular_formula`** on these 9 and record the uncertainty, on the grounds that neither value is defensible and a blank field is honest where a wrong number is not.

Neither 1 nor 2 is right in the sense of being true; they differ in which direction the error runs. My inclination is **3 for `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`** (where even MediaDive has no CAS) and **1 for the rest** (follow the source), but this publishes into `docs/data/` so it should be decided rather than assumed.

## Retitle suggestion

"9 labels state hydration numbers with no known hydrate" is still accurate; "likely sulfate→chloride slips upstream" should come out of the discussion, as it is now disproven.

Two more for this list, found from the duplicate-identifier angle (#417) rather than the hydrate-notation one. Both are sulfates, so they fall outside the 19 chlorides/phosphates checked here.

| record label | occ | stated n | known hydrates of that salt |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| `CaSO4 x 7 H2O` | 2 | 7 | ½ (bassanite), 2 (gypsum) — **no heptahydrate** |
| `K2SO4 x 7 H2O` | 1 | 7 | **none** — arcanite is anhydrous and forms no stable hydrate |

Calcium sulfate is sparingly soluble (~2 g/L) and does not form high hydrates; potassium sulfate has no hydrate at all, so `K2SO4 x 7 H2O` names a substance that cannot exist rather than one that is merely unusual.

**The same "7 H2O" pattern this issue already flags applies, and the corpus frequencies support it.** Counting hydrate suffixes across MIM:

```
x 2 H2O    20 records   12,413 occurrences
x 7 H2O    18 records    9,283      <- MgSO4 4,050 · FeSO4 2,296 · ZnSO4 2,150 · CoSO4 693
x 4 H2O     9 records    3,836
x 6 H2O    24 records    3,423
```

`x 7 H2O` is the second-commonest suffix and is almost entirely the four genuine heptahydrate sulfates that co-occur in trace-element and mineral solutions. `CaSO4 x 7 H2O` (2) and `K2SO4 x 7 H2O` (1) sit at the bottom of that same suffix group. A slip that carried "x 7 H2O" from a neighbouring MgSO4/FeSO4/ZnSO4 line onto the adjacent salt would produce exactly these — the anion-slip variant this issue proposes for `MgCl2 x 7 H2O`, one column over.

As this issue already says, that needs the source rows to confirm, not chemistry reasoning. Flagging the frequency evidence because it is consistent with the hypothesis without settling it.

Both records also carry the **anhydrous** salt's CAS (`CaSO4 x 7 H2O` → 7778-18-9, `K2SO4 x 7 H2O` → 7778-80-5), which is wrong independently of how the hydration number resolves.

Related: both are in the duplicate-identifier baseline as `HYDRATE_FAMILY_UNREVIEWED` (`CHEBI:31346`, `CHEBI:32036`), so they are also part of #321's 26.

title: 9 hydrate labels state a hydration number with no known corresponding hydrate
